title: Principality of Serbia
capsule: The Principality of Serbia (known in medieval sources as Raška) was the earliest organized Serbian polity in the central Balkans, emerging under župan leadership in the late eighth century as a semi-autonomous entity within the Byzantine and later Frankish sphere of influence. The principality expanded under Vlastimir (r. c. 830–851), who repelled Bulgarian invasion and established the ruling Vlastimirović dynasty, but thereafter repeatedly fragmented through dynastic conflict and Bulgarian overlordship. By the mid-tenth century the principality had been absorbed into the First Bulgarian Empire and then reconquered by Byzantium, ending its distinct existence before the later medieval Serbian Grand Župans reconstituted a stronger state after 1166.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Territorial extent is poorly attested; the principality's borders are reconstructed primarily from Byzantine De Administrando Imperio and archaeological inference, with considerable scholarly uncertainty.
